<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Design a pipelined 8-bit multiplier, utilizing a clock signal (clk), active low reset signal (rst_n), input enable signal (mul_en_in), and providing output enable signal (mul_en_out) and product output (mul_out).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal for chip reset.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal controlling multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input with a width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input with a width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating multiplication operation status.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output with a width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description></parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic"></logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Declare registers for input control
        reg [1:0] mul_en_in_reg;
        
        // Register for storing the multiplicand
        reg [7:0] mul_a_reg;
        // Register for storing the multiplier
        reg [7:0] mul_b_reg;
        
        // Register for storing the output enable signal
        reg [1:0] mul_en_out_reg;
        
        // Register for storing the product output
        reg [15:0] mul_out_reg;
        
        // Wire for storing temporary values during computation
        wire [7:0] temp[7:0];
        // Wire for storing the sum of partial products
        wire [15:0] sum[7:0];
        
        // Generate partial products based on the multiplier's bits
        genvar i;
        generate
            for(i = 0; i < 8; i=i+1) begin : pp_gen
                assign temp[i] = {8{mul_b_reg[i]}} & ((i == 0) ? mul_a_reg : {{(i){1'b0}}, mul_a_reg} >>> i);
            end
        endgenerate
        
        // Calculate partial sums using generated partial products
        assign sum[0] = temp[0];
        generate
            for(i = 1; i <= 7; i=i+1) begin : ps_calc
                assign sum[i] = sum[i-1] + temp[i];
            end
        endgenerate
        
        // Assign the final product output based on the output enable signal
        assign mul_out = (mul_en_out_reg[1]) ? mul_out_reg : 16'd0;
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 2'b0;
                mul_out_reg <= 16'd0;
                
                mul_en_in_reg <= 2'b0;
                mul_a_reg <= 8'd0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                // Update input enable signal
                mul_en_in_reg[0] <= mul_en_in;
                mul_en_in_reg[1] <= mul_en_in_reg[0];
                
                // Update output enable signal
                mul_en_out_reg[0] <= mul_en_in_reg[1];
                mul_en_out_reg[1] <= mul_en_out_reg[0];
                
                // Update product output
                mul_out_reg <= sum[7];
                
                // Store inputs when input enable signal is asserted
                if(mul_en_in_reg[1]) begin
                    mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                    mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>
